# Introduction

**Control structures** decide *which* code runs and *how many times*. In data management they are how you:

* check data quality before processing (`if` / `else`),
* create new categorical variables from numeric ones (`ifelse`, `switch`),
* repeat the same cleaning step on many columns, months or groups (`for`),
* skip or stop early when something is wrong (`next`, `break`),
* keep going until a condition is met, e.g. until no outliers remain (`while`, `repeat`),
* handle failures gracefully (`stop`, `warning`, `tryCatch`).



# The dataset: `airquality`

`airquality` contains daily air quality measurements in New York, May to September 1973 (153 rows). It is useful here because it has **missing values** in `Ozone` and `Solar.R`.

| Variable | Description |
 ---------- -------------
 `Ozone`    Mean ozone (ppb) 
 `Solar.R`  Solar radiation (langleys) 
 `Wind`     Average wind speed (mph) 
 `Temp`     Maximum daily temperature (°F) 
 `Month`    Month (5 to 9) 
 `Day`      Day of month 

```{r data}
aq <- airquality          # work on a copy; never modify the original
str(aq)
head(aq, 10)
summary(aq)
```

```{r missing-overview}
colSums(is.na(aq))
round(colMeans(is.na(aq)) * 100, 1)   # % missing per column
```

# Conditional statements: `if`, `else if`, `else`

## Basic syntax

```r
if (condition) {
  # runs when condition is TRUE
} else if (other_condition) {
  # runs when the first is FALSE and this is TRUE
} else {
  # runs otherwise
}
```

The `condition` must be a **single** `TRUE` or `FALSE` (a length-one logical). `NA` causes an error.

## A data-quality check

```{r if-basic}
n_missing <- sum(is.na(aq$Ozone))

if (n_missing > 0) {
  cat("Ozone has", n_missing, "missing values (",
      round(100 * n_missing / nrow(aq), 1), "%).\n")
} else {
  cat("Ozone is complete.\n")
}
```

## Several branches in a function

```{r if-elseif}
classify_temp <- function(t) {
  if (is.na(t)) {
    "Missing"
  } else if (t < 60) {
    "Cold"
  } else if (t < 80) {
    "Mild"
  } else {
    "Hot"
  }
}

classify_temp(aq$Temp[1])    # 67
classify_temp(95)
classify_temp(NA)
```

## Logical operators in conditions: `&&`, `||` vs `&`, `|`

* `&&` and `||` work on **single** values and short-circuit (the right side is skipped if the left decides the answer). Use them inside `if`.
* `&` and `|` work **element-wise** on vectors. Use them for filtering.

```{r if-operators}
x <- aq$Ozone[1:6]
x

# Element-wise: returns a vector
x > 20 & !is.na(x)

# Short-circuit: single TRUE/FALSE, safe from NA problems
val <- aq$Ozone[5]               # NA
if (!is.na(val) && val > 50) "high" else "not high / missing"
```

## Common pitfall: `if` on a vector

Since R 4.2, giving `if` a condition longer than one is an **error**. Collapse the condition with `any()`, `all()` or use `ifelse()`.

```{r if-vector-error}
res <- tryCatch(
  if (aq$Temp > 80) "hot",
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)
res

# Correct: ask a single question about the whole vector
if (any(aq$Temp > 95)) cat("At least one day exceeded 95F\n")
if (all(aq$Temp > 50))  cat("All days were above 50F\n")
```

## Useful condition helpers

```{r if-helpers}
is.na(c(1, NA, 3))
anyNA(aq$Ozone)
isTRUE(all(aq$Month %in% 5:9))      # isTRUE() guards against NA
is.numeric(aq$Temp)
is.null(NULL)
```

## Validate a data frame before working on it

```{r if-validate}
validate_airquality <- function(df) {
  required <- c("Ozone", "Solar.R", "Wind", "Temp", "Month", "Day")

  if (!is.data.frame(df)) {
    stop("Input must be a data frame.")
  }
  if (!all(required %in% names(df))) {
    missing_cols <- setdiff(required, names(df))
    stop("Missing columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }
  if (nrow(df) == 0) {
    warning("Data frame has zero rows.")
    return(FALSE)
  }
  TRUE
}

validate_airquality(aq)

tryCatch(validate_airquality(aq[, 1:3]),
         error = function(e) cat("Validation failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"))
```

# Vectorised conditionals: `ifelse()`

`ifelse(test, yes, no)` evaluates `test` for **every element** and picks `yes` or `no` for each. It is the standard way to create a new column from a condition.

## Create a categorical variable

```{r ifelse-basic}
aq$Temp_cat <- ifelse(aq$Temp < 60, "Cold",
                ifelse(aq$Temp < 80, "Mild", "Hot"))

table(aq$Temp_cat)
head(aq[, c("Temp", "Temp_cat")])
```

## Flag missing values

```{r ifelse-flag}
aq$Ozone_missing <- ifelse(is.na(aq$Ozone), "Missing", "Observed")
table(aq$Ozone_missing, aq$Month)
```

## `ifelse()` and `NA`

`NA` in the test gives `NA` in the output. Handle it explicitly:

```{r ifelse-na}
aq$Ozone_level <- ifelse(is.na(aq$Ozone), "Unknown",
                   ifelse(aq$Ozone > 70, "High",
                    ifelse(aq$Ozone > 30, "Moderate", "Low")))
table(aq$Ozone_level)
```

## Alternative for many break points: `cut()`

Deeply nested `ifelse()` calls get hard to read. For numeric ranges, `cut()` is cleaner:

```{r cut}
aq$Temp_cut <- cut(aq$Temp,
                   breaks = c(-Inf, 60, 80, Inf),
                   labels = c("Cold", "Mild", "Hot"),
                   right  = FALSE)         # intervals are [a, b)
table(aq$Temp_cut)

# Same answer as the nested ifelse
identical(as.character(aq$Temp_cut), aq$Temp_cat)
```

## Conditional subsetting: logical filters and `which()`

```{r subsetting}
# Days with ozone above 100 ppb (exclude NA explicitly)
high_ozone <- aq[!is.na(aq$Ozone) & aq$Ozone > 100,
                 c("Ozone", "Temp", "Wind", "Month", "Day")]
high_ozone

# which() ignores NA and returns row positions
which(aq$Ozone > 100)

# Without handling NA, the filter produces junk "NA rows"
nrow(aq[aq$Ozone > 100, ])               # includes NA rows!
nrow(aq[which(aq$Ozone > 100), ])        # correct

# subset() drops NA tests automatically
nrow(subset(aq, Ozone > 100 & Month == 8))
```

# Choosing among alternatives: `switch()`

`switch(EXPR, name1 = value1, name2 = value2, ..., default)` picks the branch whose name matches the string `EXPR`. If no name matches, the unnamed last argument is returned as a default.

## A function that selects a statistic by name

```{r switch-basic}
describe_col <- function(x, stat = "mean") {
  switch(stat,
    mean   = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd     = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    range  = ,                                   # fall-through: same as next line
    spread = diff(range(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    stop("Unknown statistic: '", stat, "'")      # default
  )
}

describe_col(aq$Temp, "mean")
describe_col(aq$Temp, "median")
describe_col(aq$Temp, "range")      # falls through to "spread"

tryCatch(describe_col(aq$Temp, "mode"),
         error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
```

## Recoding labels: months to periods

`switch()` handles a **single** value, so to recode a whole column, combine it with `sapply()` / `vapply()`:

```{r switch-recode}
month_to_period <- function(m) {
  switch(as.character(m),
         "5" = ,
         "6" = "Early summer",
         "7" = ,
         "8" = "Peak summer",
         "9" = "Late summer",
         NA_character_)
}

aq$Period <- vapply(aq$Month, month_to_period, FUN.VALUE = character(1))
table(aq$Month, aq$Period)
```

## Numeric `switch()`

When `EXPR` is a number, it selects by position:

```{r switch-numeric}
switch(2, "first", "second", "third")
```

(This is less readable and less safe than named alternatives. Prefer strings.)

# Loops: `for`


## Loop over columns: missing-value report

```{r for-cols}
for (col in names(airquality)) {
  n_na <- sum(is.na(airquality[[col]]))
  cat(sprintf("%-8s | missing: %3d | %5.1f%%\n",
              col, n_na, 100 * n_na / nrow(airquality)))
}
```

## Pre-allocate results, then fill

Growing a vector inside a loop (`x <- c(x, new)`) is slow. Create the container first.

```{r for-prealloc}
vars <- c("Ozone", "Solar.R", "Wind", "Temp")

col_means <- numeric(length(vars))
names(col_means) <- vars

for (i in seq_along(vars)) {
  col_means[i] <- mean(airquality[[vars[i]]], na.rm = TRUE)
}
round(col_means, 2)
```

## Loop over rows: classification

```{r for-rows}
comfort <- character(nrow(aq))      # pre-allocate

for (i in seq_len(nrow(aq))) {
  t <- aq$Temp[i]
  w <- aq$Wind[i]

  comfort[i] <- if (t >= 80 && w < 8) {
    "Hot and stuffy"
  } else if (t >= 80) {
    "Hot and breezy"
  } else if (t < 60) {
    "Cold"
  } else {
    "Comfortable"
  }
}

aq$Comfort <- comfort
table(aq$Comfort)
```

## Nested loops: a month by variable summary matrix

```{r for-nested}
months <- sort(unique(aq$Month))

summary_mat <- matrix(NA_real_,
                      nrow = length(months), ncol = length(vars),
                      dimnames = list(month.abb[months], vars))

for (m in months) {
  for (v in vars) {
    summary_mat[month.abb[m], v] <- mean(aq[aq$Month == m, v], na.rm = TRUE)
  }
}
round(summary_mat, 1)
```

## Loop over a list of data frames (split by group)

```{r for-split}
by_month <- split(aq, aq$Month)

results <- vector("list", length(by_month))
names(results) <- paste0("Month_", names(by_month))

for (nm in names(by_month)) {
  d <- by_month[[nm]]
  results[[paste0("Month_", nm)]] <- data.frame(
    month      = as.integer(nm),
    n_days     = nrow(d),
    max_temp   = max(d$Temp),
    mean_ozone = round(mean(d$Ozone, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    pct_na     = round(100 * mean(is.na(d$Ozone)), 1)
  )
}

monthly_report <- do.call(rbind, results)
rownames(monthly_report) <- NULL
monthly_report
```

## Visualising the loop result

```{r for-plot}
barplot(monthly_report$mean_ozone,
        names.arg = month.abb[monthly_report$month],
        col = "steelblue", xlab = "Month", ylab = "Mean ozone (ppb)",
        main = "Average ozone by month (missing values removed)")
```

# Controlling loops: `next` and `break`

* `next` skips the rest of the current iteration and moves on.
* `break` leaves the loop entirely.

## `next`: skip columns that don't qualify

```{r next}
# Add a text column and a logical column so the data is of mixed type
mixed <- transform(airquality, Station = "NYC", Rainy = Wind > 12)

for (col in names(mixed)) {
  if (!is.numeric(mixed[[col]])) {
    cat("Skipping non-numeric column:", col, "\n")
    next
  }
  if (!anyNA(mixed[[col]])) next          # nothing to report

  cat("Column", col, "has", sum(is.na(mixed[[col]])), "missing values\n")
}
```

## `break`: stop at the first match

```{r break}
first_high <- NA_integer_

for (i in seq_len(nrow(aq))) {
  if (is.na(aq$Ozone[i])) next            # ignore missing readings
  if (aq$Ozone[i] > 100) {
    first_high <- i
    break                                  # no need to look further
  }
}

first_high
aq[first_high, c("Ozone", "Temp", "Month", "Day")]
```

## `next` and `break` together: build a data-quality log

```{r next-break-log}
log_entries <- character(0)

for (col in names(airquality)) {
  x <- airquality[[col]]
  pct <- 100 * mean(is.na(x))

  if (pct == 0) next                                  # clean column, move on
  log_entries <- c(log_entries,
                   sprintf("%s: %.1f%% missing", col, pct))

  if (pct > 50) {                                     # unusable: stop the audit
    log_entries <- c(log_entries, "STOP: more than half missing")
    break
  }
}
log_entries
```

# Loops with conditions: `while` and `repeat`

## `while`: repeat as long as a condition holds


### Accumulate until a threshold

```{r while-accumulate}
threshold <- 2000
i <- 0
total <- 0

while (total < threshold && i < nrow(aq)) {
  i <- i + 1
  if (!is.na(aq$Ozone[i])) total <- total + aq$Ozone[i]
}

cat("Cumulative ozone first exceeded", threshold, "after", i, "days (total =", total, ")\n")
cat("That is", format(as.Date(sprintf("1973-%02d-%02d", aq$Month[i], aq$Day[i])), "%d %B"), "\n")
```

### Iterative outlier removal

Removing outliers changes the mean and standard deviation, which can expose new outliers. A `while` loop repeats until the data is stable.

```{r while-outliers}
x <- aq$Ozone[!is.na(aq$Ozone)]
n_start <- length(x)
iteration <- 0

while (length(x) > 5 && any(abs(x - mean(x)) > 2.5 * sd(x))) {
  keep <- abs(x - mean(x)) <= 2.5 * sd(x)
  cat(sprintf("Iteration %d: removing %d value(s)\n", iteration + 1, sum(!keep)))
  x <- x[keep]
  iteration <- iteration + 1
}

cat("Started with", n_start, "values, finished with", length(x),
    "after", iteration, "iteration(s)\n")
```

```{r while-outliers-plot}
boxplot(list(Original = aq$Ozone, Trimmed = x),
        col = c("tomato", "seagreen"), ylab = "Ozone (ppb)",
        main = "Ozone before and after iterative outlier trimming")
```

## `repeat`: loop forever until `break`



```{r repeat}
set.seed(123)
target   <- mean(aq$Temp)
attempts <- 0

repeat {
  attempts <- attempts + 1
  s <- sample(aq$Temp, size = 20)

  if (abs(mean(s) - target) < 0.5) break          # success

  if (attempts >= 1000) {                          # safety valve
    warning("No acceptable sample found")
    break
  }
}

cat("Found a representative sample of 20 days after", attempts, "attempt(s)\n")
cat("Population mean:", round(target, 2), "| sample mean:", round(mean(s), 2), "\n")
```

> **Always include a safety valve** (maximum iterations) in `while` / `repeat` loops that depend on data to avoid infinite loops.

# Handling problems: `stop()`, `warning()`, `tryCatch()`

Control flow is also about what happens when something goes wrong.



```{r trycatch}
safe_mean <- function(x) {
  tryCatch({
    if (!is.numeric(x)) stop("input is not numeric")
    if (all(is.na(x)))  warning("all values are NA")
    mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  },
  warning = function(w) {
    cat("  Warning caught:", conditionMessage(w), "\n")
    NA_real_
  },
  error = function(e) {
    cat("  Error caught:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
    NA_real_
  },
  finally = cat("  (checked one column)\n"))
}

test_cols <- list(Temp = aq$Temp,
                  Label = aq$Temp_cat,          # character: will error
                  AllNA = rep(NA_real_, 5))     # all NA: will warn

for (nm in names(test_cols)) {
  cat(nm, ":\n")
  print(safe_mean(test_cols[[nm]]))
}
```

# A complete example: a configurable cleaning function

This function combines **everything**: validation with `if`/`stop`, `match.arg` and `switch` to choose a strategy, a `for` loop over columns, `next` to skip, and `ifelse`/`pmin` to cap outliers.

```{r cleaning-function}
clean_airquality <- function(df,
                             method     = c("mean", "median", "drop", "none"),
                             outlier_sd = NULL,
                             verbose    = TRUE) {

  method <- match.arg(method)                       # validates the choice
  stopifnot(is.data.frame(df))                      # basic guard
  if (!is.null(outlier_sd) && outlier_sd <= 0) {
    stop("`outlier_sd` must be positive.")
  }

  id_cols <- c("Month", "Day")                      

  # Step 1: missing values 
  if (method == "drop") {
    out <- df[complete.cases(df), ]
    if (verbose) cat("Dropped", nrow(df) - nrow(out), "incomplete rows\n")
  } else {
    out <- df
    for (col in names(out)) {
      if (!is.numeric(out[[col]])) next             # skip text/logical
      if (col %in% id_cols)        next
      miss <- is.na(out[[col]])
      if (!any(miss))              next             # nothing to impute
      if (method == "none")        next

      fill <- switch(method,
                     mean   = mean(out[[col]],   na.rm = TRUE),
                     median = median(out[[col]], na.rm = TRUE))

      out[[col]][miss] <- fill
      if (verbose) {
        cat(sprintf("Imputed %2d value(s) in %-8s with %s = %.2f\n",
                    sum(miss), col, method, fill))
      }
    }
  }

  # Step 2: cap extreme values 
  if (!is.null(outlier_sd)) {
    for (col in setdiff(names(out), id_cols)) {
      if (!is.numeric(out[[col]])) next
      m <- mean(out[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
      s <- sd(out[[col]],   na.rm = TRUE)
      upper <- m + outlier_sd * s
      lower <- m - outlier_sd * s
      n_cap <- sum(out[[col]] > upper | out[[col]] < lower, na.rm = TRUE)
      if (n_cap == 0) next
      out[[col]] <- pmin(pmax(out[[col]], lower), upper)
      if (verbose) cat(sprintf("Capped %d outlier(s) in %s\n", n_cap, col))
    }
  }

  out
}
```

Try it with different strategies:

```{r cleaning-demo}
cat("--- Mean imputation + cap at 3 SD ---\n")
clean_mean <- clean_airquality(airquality, method = "mean", outlier_sd = 3)

cat("\n--- Median imputation ---\n")
clean_median <- clean_airquality(airquality, method = "median")

cat("\n--- Drop incomplete rows ---\n")
clean_drop <- clean_airquality(airquality, method = "drop")

# Compare the outcomes
comparison <- data.frame(
  Strategy     = c("Original", "Mean", "Median", "Drop"),
  Rows         = c(nrow(airquality), nrow(clean_mean), nrow(clean_median), nrow(clean_drop)),
  Missing      = c(sum(is.na(airquality)), sum(is.na(clean_mean)),
                   sum(is.na(clean_median)), sum(is.na(clean_drop))),
  Mean_Ozone   = round(c(mean(airquality$Ozone, na.rm = TRUE), mean(clean_mean$Ozone),
                         mean(clean_median$Ozone), mean(clean_drop$Ozone)), 2),
  SD_Ozone     = round(c(sd(airquality$Ozone, na.rm = TRUE), sd(clean_mean$Ozone),
                         sd(clean_median$Ozone), sd(clean_drop$Ozone)), 2)
)
comparison
```

Invalid input is caught by the control logic:

```{r cleaning-errors}
tryCatch(clean_airquality(airquality, method = "mode"),
         error = function(e) cat("Error:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"))

tryCatch(clean_airquality(list(a = 1)),
         error = function(e) cat("Error:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"))

tryCatch(clean_airquality(airquality, outlier_sd = -2),
         error = function(e) cat("Error:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"))
```

Visual check of the imputation effect:

```{r cleaning-plot}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
hist(airquality$Ozone, breaks = 20, col = "grey70", border = "white",
     main = "Original (NAs ignored)", xlab = "Ozone (ppb)")
hist(clean_mean$Ozone, breaks = 20, col = "steelblue", border = "white",
     main = "Mean-imputed + capped", xlab = "Ozone (ppb)")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

Notice the spike at the mean in the right-hand histogram: mean imputation reduces variance. That is a real trade-off to weigh when choosing the `method` argument.
